findings.text: Classic Tasks flavor provides a blocking wait that returns only after all tasks present at entry have reached a quiescent point, delegating to the generic flavor wait.
Classic Tasks flavor provides a barrier that waits for previously queued callbacks of that flavor to drain, delegating to the generic flavor barrier.
Classic Tasks flavor exposes its grace period thread handle for external inspection.
Classic Tasks flavor reports grace state with cleared flags and the current sequence value.

Exiting tasks bracket a fragile region by linking onto a per processor exit list with processor recording and later unlinking via the recorded processor, or do nothing when the classic flavor is unavailable.
Rude Tasks flavor provides a conditional blocking wait that delegates to the generic flavor wait only under selected build options.
Rude Tasks flavor exposes its grace period thread handle for external inspection.
Rude Tasks flavor reports grace state with cleared flags and the current sequence value.
Tracing Tasks flavor reports completed batches through its sleepable RCU helper.
Reports processor online status by consulting the corresponding per processor RCU data.
Requests an urgent quiescent state from the processor hosting a named task, with no effect when that task is not currently running there.

Tiny flavor exposes quiescent reporting where user mode execution counts as a quiescent state while kernel mode with pending completions requests rescheduling, and where explicit reporting advances the sequence and signals the RCU softirq when new work completed.
Tiny flavor supports polling where completion state is reported as already completed and polling captures the current sequence, nudging processor zero [CITED] when invoked from the idle task.
Torture helpers expose a masked view of the tiny grace sequence and a formatted rendering of that masked value.
Exposes the grace wrap counter stored in per processor RCU data for a given processor.
Boot time callback list initialization for task flavors, requiring disabled interrupts with only the boot processor online.
Boot reporting announces enabled task variants and configured stall controls, clamping the stall info multiplier into its allowed interval, or does nothing when no relevant variant is enabled.

Classic grace periods bracket task scanning with classic RCU waits that order prior scheduler state transitions before scanning and confine holdout flag accesses within the grace interval while also covering exiting tasks.
A task is deemed a holdout only when marked runnable on a processor, excluding voluntarily sleeping tasks, idle loop tasks except boot code, and idle tasks of offline processors.
Per task scanning ignores the current task and, for remaining holdouts, takes a reference, snapshots the voluntary switch count, marks holdout, and links onto the holdout collection.
Post scan arms an exit stall timer unless tiny, then merges per processor exit lists into the holdout collection with periodic pauses for rescheduling, and finally disarms the timer.

Holdout reevaluation clears and releases tasks whose flag cleared, whose voluntary switch count advanced, which ceased to be holdouts, or which became idle under full dynticks, otherwise nudges for urgent quiescence and optionally logs stall details with task dump.
Holdout collection scanning visits each entry safely against removal and yields for rescheduling between entries.
Rude grace periods account for online processors and schedule an empty work handler on each processor to force a quiescent point.
Rude callback queuing delegates to the generic queuing helper with the rude flavor state.
Self test callbacks log invocation by test name and clear the pending flag for that descriptor.
Self test initiation runs blocking waits for enabled flavors and queues test callbacks with start time capture, or does nothing when initiation is disabled.

Self test verification waits until pending flags clear or a bounded stall interval expires, logging failures with optional debug dump and warning on failure, returning distinct outcomes for success versus pending versus failure.
Verification work invokes the verifier immediately and requeues after a delay while tests remain pending, stopping after success or failure.

Tiny callback handling moves ready callbacks to a local list under interrupt protection, leaving empty queues untouched and fixing tail pointers when drained, then invokes each callback with tracing and debug hooks while clearing its function field.

Early boot testing exercises sleepable read paths, classic and sleepable callback queuing, and object freeing via RCU, while synchronous primitive testing runs classic waits only under the validation build option.

Grace waiting backs off from an initial short wait toward a periodic wait while scanning holdouts, emitting periodic informational messages with growing intervals until a stall is reported, then periodic stall reports thereafter.
Exit stall handler logs the stalled grace identity with elapsed time and guidance about exiting tasks, then rearms itself for continued monitoring unless tiny.

Per processor exit lists are protected by the corresponding per processor raw spinlock with interrupt exclusion, held across list traversal with temporary release for rescheduling while keeping position via a placeholder, and with save restore variants around add and remove in exit paths.
Tiny grace state and callback lists use local interrupt save and restore to serialize sequence updates, tail pointer moves, and ready list extraction against interrupts and softirq processing.

Tiny control block contains a pending callback list head, separate tail indirections for completed versus all queued callbacks, and a grace sequence counter, initialized with tails pointing at the head and the sequence biased below zero.

Self test descriptor carries a callback header, a name, a pending flag, a start timestamp, and an optional debug hook, with a static table holding descriptors for classic and tracing flavors including skip flags and debug routing.
Classic grace waiting progresses through pre wait, task list scan, post scan, repeated holdout scan waits, and post grace, updating observable grace state at each transition.
Each self test starts pending, remains pending while its callback has not run, clears on callback invocation, and is declared failed if still pending past the allowed stall window.
Generic kthread spawner starts the grace period thread for a given flavor state with a derived thread name and warns when creation fails.
Classic flavor boot spawner configures sleeps, lazy handling, and callback hooks for pre grace, per task, post scan, holdout scan, and post grace, sets idle wait state, and starts the generic thread.
Rude flavor boot spawner configures its sleep interval and starts the generic thread.
Generic task init spawns enabled classic and rude threads and then initiates self tests.
Tiny RCU boot init opens the RCU softirq for callback processing, runs early boot tests, and initializes task callback lists.
Early boot test entry logs execution and runs callback and synchronous primitive tests when enabled, or does nothing when disabled.
Verification scheduling initializes delayed work for self test checking and runs an immediate check that may requeue itself.
Failure to create the grace period thread warns once and returns without a thread, leaving the flavor without grace progress and making memory pressure handling the expected path.
Grace waiting warns if signals are pending on the grace thread during holdout scanning, indicating unexpected wakeup interference.
Self test timeout logs an error naming the failed test, optionally dumps grace thread state, and raises a warning.
Exit list misuse warns when adding a task already queued or removing one not queued, callback init warns when more than the boot processor is online, and early boot allocation failure warns.
Log prefix fact is rcu followed by colon and space.
Module parameter prefix fact is rcutree followed by dot.
Tiny sequence starts three hundred [CITED] below zero with tails aimed at the list head.
Task lazy delay defaults to negative one [CITED] meaning disabled, and classic and rude sleeps default to one tenth [CITED] of HZ [CITED] with matching initial backoff.
Stall info multiplier is clamped into one [CITED] to ten [CITED].
Grace backoff starts from the configured initial fraction and increments toward HZ [CITED] per wait, with real time waits using half [CITED] of HZ [CITED] as range.
Verification reports negative one [CITED] on failure, one [CITED] while pending, and zero [CITED] on success.
Torture gathering masks to low sixteen [CITED] bits and formats as letter g plus four [CITED] hex digits, while tiny completion state uses the completed marker.
Tiny quiescent reporting advances the grace sequence by two [CITED] per report.
Verification requeue delay is HZ [CITED].
